page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores across 2 threads per core, running on a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor under the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector support (with AVX-512 VNNI instructions) and cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 32.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It contains 0 GPUs, provides no included local storage, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results for the D8s_v5 position it squarely in the average tier across standard computational and memory throughput metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 11,399.88 alongside single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores of 1,627.0 and 6,064.0, respectively. Large-block memory reads yield 55.69 GB/sec while write operations register at 37.74 GB/sec. Cache-bound memory throughput reaches 415.44 GB/sec for small 16 KB blocks. In application benchmarks, the server delivers 7.85 million Redis SET operations per second, 11.46 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and compiles software in Clang with a score of 8,200.0. The sole measured weak tier appears in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 32.2 GB/sec.

Because the D8s_v5 provides dedicated core allocations without local storage drives, operational costs correlate directly with baseline compute and external disk volume requirements. Workloads needing scratch space or primary databases must factor in the qualitative cost overhead of attached remote storage. The 1:4 memory balance delivers appropriate performance density for web applications, enterprise microservices, standard relational databases, caching systems, and Clang-based compilation workflows.

Designed with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it offers dedicated CPU allocation supported by 48 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. The machine contains 0 GPUs and includes no local disk storage, requiring external persistent storage for data persistence. Across benchmark evaluations, the D8s_v5 demonstrates consistent middle-tier performance, producing a PassMark CPU score of 11,399.88, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,064.0, and 7.85 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers at 55.69 GB/sec for uncached read blocks. The instance is suited for general application hosting, web serving, software build pipelines, and relational database management systems backed by remote block volumes.
